title: Per-tenant priority coalescer and adaptive watermark for console metrics ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We are seeing high variance in per-tenant ingest patterns: a small fraction of tenants produce hotkeys and bursty streams that dominate processing latency and memory. The goal of this ticket is to implement a per-tenant priority coalescer that groups short-window metric writes into adaptive windows with tenant-aware watermarks. The coalescer will: (1) maintain short, high-priority micro-windows for latency-sensitive tenants, (2) fall back to coalesced, lower-resolution windows for noisy/high-cardinality tenants to protect downstream state and CPU, and (3) emit backpressure signals to the edge if in-flight partition queues exceed soft thresholds. This is an ingest-side streaming processor change (queue/stream processors) intended to reduce end-to-end p95/p99 write latency, lower memory pressure at the aggregator stage, and enable graceful degradation rather than dropping tenant data.
acceptance_criteria: p95 end-to-end latency for typical tenants improves by at least 20% under representative load compared to baseline ingest pipeline
system remains below 70% memory utilization on aggregator nodes for 99% of test runs with synthetic hotkeys that previously pushed it above 95%
coalesced events retain an explicit resolution tag so downstream consumers can reconstruct or ignore aggregated samples
backpressure signals are emitted and respected by edge clients in test harness (simulate signal -> reduced ingress rate)
feature flag gates the coalescer with a canary cohort (10% of tenants) and rollback toggles available
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Spec drafted and synced with PM/Observability. Collected example tenant traces and hotkey heatmaps.
2026-02-26: Prototype of the coalescer in the local stream simulator. Verified basic correctness for coalescing and resolution tagging.
2026-03-03: Integration test harness added that replays production traces; found a correctness issue with late-arriving events causing duplicate aggregates — added per-window dedupe IDs.
2026-03-10: Per-tenant config store integration merged (allows per-tenant min-window and priority overrides). Running internal canary on staging.
2026-03-12: Observability instrumentation added for per-window latency and memory sketches. Preparing load test runs against aggregated pipeline.
rollout_plan: Gate behind runtime feature flag with per-tenant override (default off)
Canary cohort: enable for 10% low-risk tenants for 48 hours, validate latency and memory metrics
Stage: increase to 30% including some mid-volume tenants for 72 hours
Full rollout: enable-by-default and monitor SLOs for 7 days
Rollback: flip feature flag off immediately if p99 ingestion latency or error rate regression > 25%
test_plan: Unit tests for window boundary computation, dedupe ID generation, and resolution tagging
Integration tests replaying anonymized production traces with variable skew/late-arrival scenarios
Load tests simulating 10k tenants with a heavy-tail distribution of hotkeys to reproduce memory pressure
Chaos test: inject network flaps and broker partition rebalances to ensure idempotent aggregates
End-to-end acceptance: confirm downstream dashboards and billing pipelines consume resolution-tagged aggregates without loss
notes: Trade-offs: we coalesce to protect the aggregator at the cost of higher downstream reconstruction complexity; added resolution tag is required for consumers that need raw granularity.
Decision: Grouping is time-window + tenant-priority based rather than only count-based because time windows map better to our SLA guarantees.
Follow-ups: explore combining coalescer with adaptive sketch-based pre-aggregation for extremely high-cardinality tenants (future ticket).
Risk: if per-tenant config becomes large, the coalescer must shard config lookups; we included a local LRU config cache in the design.
